newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-TENDINITIS FORCES BECKER OUT OF EC EVENT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TENDINITIS FORCES BECKER OUT OF EC EVENT.

text.p: Fourth seed Boris Becker pulled out of the European Community championship on Tuesday because of tendinitis, an ATP spokeswoman said.
"Boris Becker pulled out, just now. He has...tendinitis in the wrist," she said.

"On Sunday I was pain free but last night the pain came back a little," Becker told a brief news conference. "This morning I had to stop practising after 35 minutes. It was as bad as in Dubai," he said.

Antwerp tournament director Georges Baudeweyns had said on Monday that Becker had recovered from the wrist injury which forced him out of last week's Dubai Open before his quarter-final against Goran Ivanisevic.
Becker, who was to have played Czech Petr Korda in the first round of the Antwerp event on Wednesday, will be replaced by lucky loser Dennis van Scheppingen of the Netherlands.
"It's tendinitis. All the bones are fine," Becker said. "It's a question of time. I can't say whether it will take eight days or two weeks."
He said he was hoping to resume practising this weekend and take part in the Italian Indoor in Milan.
He said he had been told by doctors that the problem originated from a pinched nerve in his neck.
"But now the inflammation is in that particular spot," he said.
